questions.q: What are FILTER's three arguments, in order?
options: range, criteria, sum_range
array, include, [if_empty]
array, sort_index, sort_order
lookup_value, array, if_not_found
questions.explain: FILTER takes the array to pull rows from, a boolean include condition built from a same-height range, and an optional if_empty fallback.

questions.q: In =SORT(D2:D11,1,-1), what does the 1 refer to, and what does -1 mean?
options: The 1 is a typo and has no function
Both numbers refer to sheet row numbers
The 1 means ascending order and the -1 is the column index
The 1 is the sort column/row within the array itself (not sheet column A), and -1 means descending order
questions.explain: sort_index counts columns (or rows) within the array argument itself, and sort_order is 1 for ascending or -1 for descending.

questions.q: What does setting UNIQUE's exactly_once argument to TRUE change?
options: It limits the result to a single cell
It has no effect on the result
It returns only values that appear exactly one time in the range, excluding anything with duplicates
It sorts the unique values alphabetically
questions.explain: exactly_once filters the result down to values with no duplicates at all — genuinely different from a plain distinct-values list.

questions.q: How do you combine two conditions with AND logic inside a single FILTER's include argument (without a helper column)?
options: FILTER cannot combine more than one condition
Multiply the two condition arrays together with *
Add the two condition arrays together with +
Separate them with a comma as a fourth argument
questions.explain: Multiplying two TRUE/FALSE arrays with * works like AND (both must be TRUE/1); adding them with + works like OR.

options: SORT runs first, then UNIQUE removes duplicates from the sorted result
Excel throws an error because functions can't be nested this way
Both functions run simultaneously and average their results
UNIQUE runs first, producing a deduplicated array that SORT then reorders — no intermediate cell is ever created on the sheet
questions.explain: Nested dynamic array functions evaluate inside-out just like any nested formula — UNIQUE's spilled array becomes SORT's array argument directly, in memory.
